newsitem.title: USA: AOL sets $50 million pact with CUC, others seen.
newsitem.headline: AOL sets $50 million pact with CUC, others seen.

text.p: America Online Inc. and the huge marketing company CUC International Inc. Tuesday agreed to a deal to put CUC's shopping, travel and other merchandising services in prominent locations on AOL's growing network.
The world's largest online service will receive at least $50 million under the three-year marketing agreement, which could be worth more from revenue sharing, the companies said.

Under the deal, CUC will allow AOL's 8 million subscribers to buy goods and services at discounts through CUC's new Internet commerce site, called NetMarket. CUC will also have the anchor tenancy of AOL's new Shopping Channel.
AOL members will be able to purchase goods through CUC's Shoppers Advantage, Travelers Advantage, Auto Vantage and other discount clubs, the companies said.

As AOL continues to move toward getting more sales from advertising and merchandising, International Business Machines Corp. said Tuesday it will shut down its World Avenue virtual shopping mall on the Internet.

"Like real estate, electronic commerce is all about location, location, location," Bob Pittman, president of AOL Networks, said by telephone. "In the online market, if you have a nifty store and it's off in the woods somewhere, it's not going as well as a nifty store that is on the corner of 5th Avenue and 57th Street."

CUC, a direct marketing powerhouse, last month agreed to a $10.9 billion merger with HFS Inc., a franchiser whose brands include Ramada Inn, Century 21 Real Estate, Howard Johnson, Avis and Coldwell Banker.

The deal expands on CUC's current partnership with AOL, since it co-brands some of its products with AOL. For example, its Travel Advantage programme is a mainstay of AOL's travel channel. Jamie Kiggen, a Cowen & Co. analyst, said CUC is one of AOL's $1 million-per-year advertisers.

The company, based in Stamford, Conn., offers coupon books as well as traveller and shopper clubs to its members, who pay an annual fee to buy goods and services at discount rates. CUC has recently been trying to develop more online revenue, and the agreement with AOL is a step in that direction.

While AOL, based in Dulles, Va., dominates its online competitors such as CompuServe Corp., the Microsoft Network, and Prodigy Inc., it has been seeking to expand its revenue sources. It now charges subscribers a flat rate of $19.95 a month for unlimited access to AOL and the Internet.

One way is to offer consumers products and services online since online providers typically get fees based on the transactions. In a deal signed with Tel-Save in February, AOL got an upfront payment of $100 million while TelSave got access to market its long-distance telephone service to AOL's members.

In its third quarter, AOL saw a big increase in its non-subscription revenues to $74.7 million, with advertising and electronic commerce revenues of $60.7 million, up 37 percent from the previous quarter.
AOL said it plans to do more similar deals like the CUC and Tel-Save marketing deals.

"Clearly, this is a way of doing business and there are other people interested in the online world," Pittman said. "This is not an anomaly. You should expect this as the way business will be conducted."

The marketing pact with CUC could bring about a million new shopping club memberships to CUC, based on CUC's promotions, direct mail and telemarketing activities. A CUC spkoesman said CUC has 350,000 to 400,000 online members out of 68 million total members.
AOL's stock rose $3.125 to $60.50 and CUC added 50 cents to $24.125, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
